meta.title: Operation Glass House: The NCII Siege
meta.summary: A ransomware group has breached a critical infrastructure node. They are moving from data theft to physical intimidation and public psychological warfare.

questions.text: Early telemetry shows rapid encryption on back-office servers. IT requests a 'Total Isolation' protocol, cutting all internet-facing services immediately.
questions.context: Isolation stops the spread but halts public services and $5M in hourly revenue.

answers.label: Total Isolation
answers.description: Cut all gateways. Prioritize containment above all else.
answers.boardReading: Safety-first, but causes immediate national disruption.
answers.consequence: Breach is contained, but the public starts to panic as services go dark.

answers.label: Partial Isolation
answers.description: Block only known malicious IPs while keeping core services running.
answers.boardReading: Risky middle ground; may allow exfiltration to continue.
answers.consequence: Services remain up, but 200GB of sensitive data is exfiltrated.

answers.label: Passive Observation
answers.description: Trace the actor's path without interfering to identify the source.
answers.boardReading: Highly aggressive intel gathering; dangerous if detected.
answers.consequence: You identify the actor, but they trigger a wiper script in retaliation.

questions.text: The actor confirms they have exfiltrated the Board's internal salary records and personal emails. They demand $5M to 'delete' the data.
questions.context: Payment funds crime; refusal guarantees a public leak.

answers.label: Absolute Refusal
answers.description: Maintain no-pay policy and prepare for the leak.
answers.boardReading: Principles over reputation. Protects national deterrence.
answers.consequence: The actor leaks the data; Board members face intense public scrutiny.

answers.label: Negotiate to Buy Time
answers.description: Engage a negotiator to stall while teams try to locate the leak source.
answers.boardReading: Tactical pragmatism. Buys time for response coordination.
answers.consequence: Stalling works for 12 hours, allowing a forensic snapshot to complete.

answers.label: Quiet Payment
answers.description: Pay the ransom immediately using private insurance.
answers.boardReading: Expedient but creates 'moral hazard'. Attacker now knows you pay.
answers.consequence: Data is deleted, but the actor returns a month later with a new demand.

questions.text: WILDCARD : Attackers send photos of Board members' children to their personal phones, demanding immediate payment.
questions.context: A life-safety issue exceeding standard cyber protocols.

answers.label: State Security Escalation
answers.description: Engage high-level Police and Intel agencies for home protection.
answers.boardReading: Correct protocol. Moves safety into the domain of state protection.
answers.consequence: Families are secured, but news begins to leak through police channels.

answers.label: Private Security
answers.description: Hire private tactical teams without alerting the state.
answers.boardReading: Insular. Risks miscommunication with official law enforcement.
answers.consequence: Security is tight but the actor retaliates with more data leaks.

answers.label: Strategic Surrender
answers.description: Publicly announce you are paying under duress to save lives.
answers.boardReading: Human-centric but catastrophic for national deterrence.
answers.consequence: Lives are saved, but the nation is viewed as vulnerable to extortion.

questions.text: WILDCARD : A whistleblower site publishes the earlier Board minutes. Press is demanding an interview.
questions.context: The narrative is slipping; a posture must be chosen.

answers.label: The 'Full Truth' Presser
answers.description: Host a live conference. Admit the breach and the personal threats.
answers.consequence: Initial shock gives way to massive public support against the attackers.

answers.label: Strict Legal Denial
answers.description: Issue a written statement denying the 'rumours'.
answers.boardReading: Old-school 'Deny and Deflect'. High risk of being caught lying.
answers.consequence: Whistleblower releases audio proof. Public trust collapses instantly.

answers.label: Managed Leak
answers.description: Selectively brief one high-tier journalist to frame the org as victim.
answers.boardReading: Strategic communications. Aims to control the narrative tempo.
answers.consequence: Coverage is fair, but other media outlets turn hostile.

questions.text: Agencies offer to conduct an 'Offensive Cyber Operation' against the attackers using company systems.
questions.context: A 'hack back'. Effective but legally complex.

answers.label: Authorize Full State Access
answers.description: Collaborate fully with the state to strike back.
answers.boardReading: Whole-of-government defense. Potent but creates state dependency.
answers.consequence: Attackers' infrastructure is destroyed, but int'l tensions rise.

answers.label: Refuse State Access
answers.boardReading: Protects neutrality. Risks being left alone for the next wave.
answers.consequence: The state cannot act. The actor pivots to target your suppliers.

answers.label: Limited Assistance
answers.description: Provide data and logs but refuse to host offensive tools.
answers.consequence: Investigation moves slowly; actor is not neutralized.

questions.text: The threat is over. Do you restore to original speed or invest in 'Security-by-Design'?
questions.context: Security slows operations; speed leaves you vulnerable.

answers.label: Security-by-Design
answers.description: Implement zero-trust. Accept a 15% operational speed drop.
answers.consequence: Org is now most secure in sector; reputation leader.

answers.label: Rapid Restoration
answers.description: Get services back to 100% capacity in 24h.
answers.boardReading: Short-sighted. Puts market share above org safety.
answers.consequence: Confidence returns briefly; a new attack succeeds in 48h.

answers.label: Outsourced Resilience
answers.description: Migrate core infra to a managed secure cloud.
answers.boardReading: Risk transfer. Efficient but creates vendor dependency.
answers.consequence: Security improves but you lose granular control.
